::: {#brief .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-sb-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The brief</p>
<dl class="lx-sb-facts">
<div><dt>The system</dt><dd>The Plains Grid (fictional): <b>Wind Ridge</b>, <b>Prairie Town</b> and <b>Metro</b> in a row, joined by two links; 4,000 MW at the 2025 peak, with real 2025 hourly shapes.</dd></div>
<div><dt>You decide</dt><dd>The day or week; a large load (a data center) and where it connects; the two link limits (MW); the <span class="lx-term" data-term="reserves">reserve</span> required; the gas price.</dd></div>
<div><dt>The engine works out</dt><dd>Each day, a <span class="lx-term" data-term="mixed-integer-program">mixed-integer program</span> <span class="lx-term" data-term="unit-commitment">commits</span> the plants (chooses which are on each hour); then a <span class="lx-term" data-term="linear-program">linear program</span> with that commitment fixed prices each zone.</dd></div>
<div><dt>It leaves out</dt><dd>Power-flow physics (a <span class="lx-term" data-term="transport-model">transport model</span>), losses, ramp limits, forecast errors, plant outages, whether the reserve can reach each zone, and prices from the mixed-integer program itself.</dd></div>
</dl>
<p class="lx-hint">Open-ended: start from a preset, change one thing at a time, and copy the plan link to keep a plan.</p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#explain .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## How the engine works, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="sb2-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Commit</dt><dd>A <span class="lx-term" data-term="mixed-integer-program">mixed-integer program</span> chooses how many units of each group are on in each hour, with minimum outputs, start-up costs and minimum run times; it shows no prices.</dd>
<dt>Price</dt><dd>With every on/off decision fixed, the dispatch linear program runs the day again; each zone's <span class="lx-term" data-term="shadow-price">shadow price</span> is its price, conditional on the commitment.</dd>
<dt>It holds when</dt><dd>The zones share 2025's weather, each link carries any flow up to its limit, each day is committed alone with its load, wind and sun known, and units never fail.</dd>
<dt>It leaves out</dt><dd>Power-flow physics, losses, ramp limits, forecast errors, outages, whether the region-wide reserve can reach a zone, and the next day when a day is committed.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The models behind the bench</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

[M2](m02-unit-commitment.html) writes unit commitment down and grows its branch-and-bound tree; [M1](m01-dispatch-to-lmp.html) reads prices from a dispatch linear program and adds the network. M2's notebook rebuilds the commitment and the conditional prices in Python. The capstone [C2](c2-plains-grid-hard-year.html) runs this engine over a year and checks adequacy.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>The days and weeks you can run</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts">
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Period</th><th scope="col">Why this one</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Summer peak day, 29 July 2025</td><td>The 2025 summer day with the highest hourly demand</td></tr>
<tr><td>Winter peak day, 21 January 2025</td><td>The 2025 winter day with the highest hourly demand, among days with no repaired hours</td></tr>
<tr><td>Windy spring day, 17 April 2025</td><td>The 2025 spring day with the most wind energy</td></tr>
<tr><td>Peak-demand week, 14–20 August 2025</td><td>The 2025 week with the highest average daily demand peak</td></tr>
<tr><td>Low-wind winter week, 2–8 January 2025</td><td>One of the two calmest weeks of winter 2025 by mean wind; lesson A8's week</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<p>A week runs day by day: each day is committed without seeing the next, as a day-ahead market commits one day at a time, and carries the units' state at 23:00 into the next day.</p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>When two answers cost the same: the tie rule</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<p>Several schedules can cost exactly the same. Tiny stated costs, far below a cent per MWh, pick one:</p>
<ul class="sb2-rules">
<li>Spilled wind and sun: Wind Ridge's first, then Prairie Town's, then Metro's.</li>
<li>Unserved load, if several zones could go short: Metro's first, then Prairie Town's, then Wind Ridge's.</li>
<li>Reserve: carried first by the unit groups listed first.</li>
</ul>
<p>The engine's test runs seven benchmark plans again with the tie weights ×10 and ×0.1: every number shown stays the same.</p>
<p>In those runs, each price equals the cost slope when its zone's load moves 0.001 MWh up and when it moves down: no price sits on a corner. Your own plans are not checked this way.</p>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

<li>EIA. <a href="https://www.eia.gov/electricity/gridmonitor/">Hourly Electric Grid Monitor</a> (Form EIA-930): the Southwest Power Pool's demand, wind and sun, 2025.</li>
<li>EIA. <a href="https://www.eia.gov/electricity/annual/html/epa_07_04.html">Electric Power Annual, Table 7.4</a>: average cost of fossil fuels for the electric power industry, 2025.</li>
<li>EIA. <a href="https://www.eia.gov/electricity/annual/html/epa_08_01.html">Electric Power Annual, Table 8.1</a>: average operating heat rates, 2025.</li>
<li>EIA. <a href="https://www.eia.gov/environment/emissions/co2_vol_mass.php">Carbon Dioxide Emissions Coefficients</a>.</li>
<li>HiGHS. <a href="https://ergo-code.github.io/HiGHS/dev/">Documentation</a> of the open-source solver that runs the bench in your browser.</li>
</ul>
</div>
